messages:
Maria Chen: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to agree on the migration path from global API keys to scoped API keys + RBAC. Short thread to capture decisions and blockers.

Devin Park: thanks. main ask: how do we handle existing keys in the wild? we can't force immediate regen for all customers.

Samir Patel: proposal: keep legacy keys working but treat them as org-scoped by default (least privilege) and issue short-lived scoped tokens behind an exchange endpoint. apps can call `/v1/token/exchange` with proof to get ephemeral tokens.

Chandra Iyer: +1 to exchange endpoint. we should require client auth for exchange (signed request or mTLS) for service-to-service flows. otherwise attackers can trade stolen keys for tokens with broader scope.

Maria Chen: concrete migration phases: 1) introduce `scope` field on `service_accounts` (db migration), 2) implement exchange endpoint + introspection, 3) shadow-evaluate scoped policy enforcement, 4) opt-in rollout for customers, 5) enforced for new keys, 6) mandatory after 90d.

Devin Park: DB migration needs a backfill strategy. existing rows get `scope=org:<org_id>` by default. what about project-scoped apps? some customers use project-level tokens today.

Samir Patel: we can infer project scope from token metadata if present, else fallback to org-level. add a `legacy_scope_inferred` flag during backfill so we can track which tokens were guessed.

Chandra Iyer: auditing & telemetry: we must tag each token exchange event with original api_key id and IP. also surface drift metrics: % of requests using legacy vs scoped.

Maria Chen: authz model: three primitives — role bindings, resource scopes (org/project), and delegation chains (svc->svc). roles remain same (admin/editor/viewer) but evaluation logic must short-circuit on explicit deny.

Devin Park: runtime perf concern: introspection on every request is expensive. caching TTL and cache invalidation on rotation. recommend per-key cache with TTL 60s and invalidation via pub/sub on rotation.

Samir Patel: note on token format: prefer JWT for signed claims for cross-region validation, but use opaque tokens for exchange responses internally. JWTs complicate rotation unless we publish jwks and implement kid logic.

Chandra Iyer: mTLS for infra services + signed JWTs for external clients. keep exchange returns opaque short-lived bearer tokens for internal usage.

Maria Chen: compatibility toggle plan: runtime flag `AUTHZ_STRICT_SCOPING` default false. when true, reject non-scoped tokens. ops can flip post-rollout.

Devin Park: SDK changes: add `Auth.exchangeForScopedToken()` helper, automatic retry on 401 with exchange flow, and telemetry hooks. devex needs a migration guide.

Samir Patel: code sketch for claim shape: `{
  "sub": "svc:123",
  "iss": "redwood",
  "scopes": ["org:acme:read","project:acme:billing:write"]}` — keep `actor_type` and `delegated_by` optional.

Chandra Iyer: security checklist items: rotation policy (90d for long-lived), ephemeral TTL (15m), revoke endpoint, admin UI to search by original api_key id. also rate-limit token exchanges to avoid abuse.

Maria Chen: follow-ups: Samir to draft exchange API spec (end of week), Devin to list SDK surface changes, Chandra to draft security checklist and telemetry queries. I'll schedule a sync Wed 10am to approve rollout plan.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: canary auth-service v2 deployed to prod-canary at 3532110400 :rocket:

Devin Park: saw canary. testing exchange latency now (p50 ~12ms, p95 ~48ms). caching will help p95.

Samir Patel: added an initial OpenAPI snippet to the RFC doc: `POST /v1/token/exchange { api_key: <string>, requested_scopes: [] }` — we'll refine request assertions.

Chandra Iyer: one open question: do we allow retroactive narrowing of an existing legacy key's scope (breaking change)? my take: we should not silently narrow; instead notify owners and create a new scoped key for them.

Maria Chen: agreed. no silent narrowing. we can offer a migration helper that spins up a scoped key and copies bindings, then notify.

Samir Patel: noted. I'll include migration helper API in spec.

Maria Chen: thanks everyone. agenda for Wed: finalize DB schema migration steps, rollback plan, and telemetry dashboards to monitor adoption.

Devin Park: +1. I'll stub dashboards in Grafana and share links before sync.

Chandra Iyer: will add threat models for the exchange endpoint.

Maria Chen: closing thread — leaving notes in RFC doc and KCD. :white_check_mark:
